acceptance_criteria.criterion: `dotnet run --project src/VideoIndexer.App` opens an empty themed Avalonia main window.
On first launch, `<ApplicationData>/VideoIndexer/appsettings.json` is created with the documented default schema (Logging / Appearance / Window / ExternalTools).
Editing `Appearance.Theme` to `Light` or `Dark` and relaunching applies the chosen variant to the main window.
A log file `<ApplicationData>/VideoIndexer/logs/videoindexer-YYYYMMDD.log` appears after launch, and changing `Logging.Verbosity` from `2` to `3` produces visibly more entries on the next run.
The App project references no MySqlConnector, Dapper, LibVLCSharp, or FFMpeg* packages.

summary: Created VideoIndexer.App.csproj: net8.0, WinExe, Avalonia 11.2.5, CommunityToolkit.Mvvm 8.3.2, Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting 8.0.1, Serilog.Extensions.Hosting, references Core + Infrastructure.

Program.cs: early AppPaths + JsonSettingsService init, EnsureDefaultSettingsFile writes embedded appsettings.json on first run, Generic Host builds DI container (IAppPaths, ISettingsService, IThemeService, Serilog, MVVM types), Avalonia started via StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime.
App.axaml: FluentTheme declared, ViewLocator as DataTemplate.

ViewLocator.cs: namespace-convention-based view resolution via DI.

comments.note: Program.cs creates AppPaths and JsonSettingsService outside DI (early init pattern) then registers them as singleton instances. This means the IConfiguration reload (reloadOnChange:true) and ISettingsService.Current can drift if settings change at runtime. A future improvement: wire IOptionsMonitor<AppOptions> to JsonSettingsService so Current stays in sync.

App.Services is a static IServiceProvider property on the App class. This is the standard Avalonia+DI bridge but makes unit testing App harder. Future milestones should consider dependency injection via constructor/interface for App-level services instead of a service locator.

ViewLocator uses namespace string replacement to find views. If the ViewModels or Views namespaces change, the locator breaks silently (returns a TextBlock error message instead of throwing). Consider adding a startup-time validation or unit test that verifies all registered ViewModels have corresponding View registrations.

MainWindow has two constructors: parameterless (for Avalonia XAML runtime loader) and DI constructor. The parameterless one leaves DataContext null; only the DI constructor sets it. If MainWindow is ever instantiated without DI (e.g., in a designer), bindings will silently fail. Acceptable for M1 where the designer is not used.

summary: Reviewed 10 modified/created files across VideoIndexer.App, VideoIndexer.Infrastructure (Settings, Logging, Theme, AppPaths). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Low, 1 Info. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Low — A05/A09 (Security Misconfiguration / Logging Failures): src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Logging/LoggingSetup.cs line 31 — options.Logging.FilePath is taken directly from user settings and passed to Serilog WriteTo.File() without validation. A tampered settings file (e.g., by local malware) could redirect log output to a UNC/SMB share, leaking log entries to a remote host or triggering an NTLM credential capture. Remediation: validate that FilePath, when set, is a rooted local path (not a UNC path) using Path.IsPathRooted() and !FilePath.StartsWith(@"\\\\"). Desktop single-user threat model keeps this Low.

Info — A04 (Insecure Design, future risk): src/VideoIndexer.App/Assets/appsettings.json contains MySqlBinaryFolder and VlcExecutablePath fields. Future milestones that spawn external processes from these user-controlled paths must canonicalize and validate the paths against known safe directories (e.g., Program Files) to prevent binary planting / DLL hijacking. No current exploit surface — noting for future implementation guidance.

Architecture is clean and appropriate for an M1 foundation WP. No blocking issues found.

Design decisions (early-init pattern, static service locator, dual constructors, sync-on-async in ThemeService.Set) are all documented inline with accurate rationale. Compiled bindings (AvaloniaUseCompiledBindingsByDefault + x:DataType), source generators ([ObservableProperty]), interface-based DI, sealed leaf types, atomic settings write via temp-file + File.Move — all idiomatic and correct.

comments.note: Program.cs earlySettings uses NullLogger<JsonSettingsService>.Instance. If LoadOrInitialise() encounters a corrupted settings file in the narrow window after EnsureDefaultSettingsFile completes, the warning log is silently dropped. Probability is negligible on first run, but the correct fix is to either use a bootstrap logger or defer earlySettings construction until after Serilog is configured. Non-blocking for M1.

ViewLocator.Build() falls back to a TextBlock when the view type is not found in the assembly, but will throw InvalidOperationException (unhandled) if the type exists in the assembly but is not registered in the DI container. The error TextBlock only guards the reflection path, not the DI path. Acceptable for M1 (one registered view), but the distinction should be understood before adding more views — consider a try/catch around GetRequiredService that returns the error TextBlock instead.

[documentation-forward] The DI bootstrap sequence in Program.cs (early AppPaths + JsonSettingsService init outside DI → host build → App.Services assignment → StartWithClassicDesktopLifetime) is non-obvious. The README or a developer docs page should include an architecture diagram or prose description of this startup flow so future contributors understand why the early-init pattern exists and what the trade-offs are.

No blocking issues found. Code quality is high for a foundation WP — clean separation of concerns, correct use of C# records for settings, atomic file writes, and all prior Developer and Security Auditor observations are accurately documented.
